findings.issue: [defect, re-verified at HEAD] A replayed identical RequestApplicationShutdown overwrites the stored OperationState with a fresh 'intent retained' one, erasing a recorded outcome that shutdown_owned will not write again.
findings.recommended: Create the OperationState only when command_id is absent; extend the replay test in tests/supervisor/test_shutdown.py.

findings.issue: [defect, partly re-verified] _forward_tracking_release retries only TimeoutError/OSError/RuntimeError, but a real grpc.aio failure is AioRpcError (no RpcError handling exists in supervisor/), so it escapes the retry loop instead of ending in TRACKING_RELEASE_UNCONFIRMED. No test covers it.
findings.recommended: Map grpc.RpcError to the retried classes in GrpcOutbound.confirm_tracking_cleanup; add retry-then-accept, retry-until-deadline and non-retryable tests in tests/supervisor/test_recovery.py.

findings.issue: [defect in parser, re-verified] A line that makes json.loads raise RecursionError (deep nesting inside the size limit) or a readline OSError kills the reader thread silently, so no channel-lost marker is queued.
findings.recommended: Catch RecursionError/OSError/ValueError in the reader loop and report via lost(); add a deep-nesting case to the parse test.

findings.issue: Ruff selects only E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B and passes cleanly (794 files formatted). Extra rules would catch the main risk classes found above on every future change at no model cost: S110/S112 (silent except), RUF006 (dropped task), ASYNC, RUF100. BLE001 would flag ~220 sites today and needs a per-site policy first.
findings.recommended: Owner to decide whether to enable S110, S112, RUF006, ASYNC1xx and RUF100 now (and BLE001 later) so a daily lint run keeps up with code changes.

findings.issue: [concern, re-read at HEAD] Acquisition worker cleanup and Visual Stimulus worker cleanup run sequentially against one deadline, so a stalled acquisition cleanup can leave the renderer's outputs unattempted.

findings.locations: acquisition/transport/services.py:69; acquisition/worker/service.py:86; visual_stimulus/transport/boundary.py:92 (and the supervisor/controller services)
findings.issue: [improvement, files changed since review] Seven handlers each re-implement the peer-authentication step (token lookup by role+generation, role/source check, abort PERMISSION_DENIED); error text and None handling differ slightly.
findings.recommended: Add one async authenticate_peer(...) beside require_authenticated_peer in shared/auth.py; keep each backend's role sets and codes.

findings.issue: [improvement, partly re-checked] Both backends hand-write the same Python-worker handshake (PlanLaunch, job, suspended create, ConfirmLaunch, resume, bootstrap, GetLaunchState poll) and the worker-side registration and descriptor validation. The copies already diverged: acquisition retains the child/job handles on failure, Visual Stimulus does not release them if launch_renderer fails after launch_suspended. (The missing-child-token defect from the first review was fixed in commit aff8e0c.)
findings.recommended: Move plan/confirm/wait-registered and the worker-side registration into one shared helper with a single failure-path handle rule; keep each backend's descriptor fields.

findings.issue: [defect, re-verified at HEAD] Visual Stimulus requires supervisor/coordinator endpoints to start with 127.0.0.1:; the acquisition worker bootstrap has no such check and then opens insecure channels carrying its credential. E08 limits rig gRPC to loopback.
findings.recommended: Apply the same loopback check in the acquisition decoder, ideally through one shared validator.

findings.issue: [defect, re-verified at HEAD] VisualStimulusFilePolicies.contract_version is set by the loader but never checked; acquisition rejects Setup when its version is absent or different.
findings.recommended: Check contract_version == 1 when Visual Stimulus admits Setup, or remove the field if no check is intended.

findings.issue: [concern, files changed] The launcher (and the client CLI) read backend TOML with plain tomllib and re-implement the policy_version and rpc.port checks, bypassing load_pair's byte limit, key allowlist and format_version check.
findings.recommended: Read rpc.port through shared/config's reader and port validator.

findings.issue: [improvement, files changed] Controller metadata uses os.name == 'nt' while every other module uses sys.platform, which is what the win32 static check narrows on; entry points call msvcrt.open_osfhandle directly instead of platform/windows.
findings.recommended: Use sys.platform consistently; add one open_inherited_handle helper under platform/windows.

findings.issue: [improvement] perf_counter_ns is used directly (grep finds 39 perf_counter references; only deadline/default-clock uses matter) instead of host_time_ns() from shared/clock.py, which E08 defines as the host clock.
findings.recommended: Use host_time_ns for deadline checks and default clocks; leave pure duration timing alone.

findings.issue: [observed] stdlib logging.getLogger is used at exactly three sites (controller recovery and acquisition preview windows); everything else reports through the JSON log/incident paths. Two of the sites sit in swallow handlers.
findings.recommended: Route through the shared incident/emergency path, or document the exception.
